headline: Hormuz shock, bond revolts and a Taiwan quarantine lock the world into stagflation

events: Iran-Israel escalation spills into Gulf: drone strikes on tankers and Ras Tanura; Brent spikes to $135 and holds above $105 for months
Strong El Nino brings record heat; Indian wheat and Southeast Asian rice failures trigger export bans and a food-price surge
Weak 10-year US Treasury auction and term-premium blowout push yields above 5.8%; Fed halts QT and opens a standing Treasury repo backstop
UK gilt rout forces emergency budget; France spreads hit 190bp, ECB activates TPI for the first time
Egypt and Pakistan miss payments; IMF resources stretched as US cuts contributions
Global stagflationary recession: world growth 0.6%, G20 inflation peaks at 7.2%
Japan JGB 30-year yield crosses 4.5%; BoJ resumes unlimited purchases, yen hits 190 per dollar before coordinated intervention
US election fought on prices and debt; winning administration imposes 'national security' tariffs on all Chinese and many allied goods, sparking EU and Mexican retaliation
Kenya, Bolivia, Argentina, Nigeria and Sri Lanka enter default or distressed restructuring; Common Framework effectively collapses
AI capex bubble deflates: two hyperscalers cut data-centre spending 35%, Nasdaq falls 38%
China declares a 'customs quarantine' around Taiwan; chip shipments disrupted for 11 weeks, global electronics and auto output plunge
US and allies impose sweeping financial sanctions on Chinese banks; dual payment systems harden, trade fragmentation index jumps
Global unemployment peaks at 6.4%; youth unemployment above 25% in North Africa and South Asia drives mass migration toward Europe
Category-5 hurricane season and Mediterranean megafires strain insurers; Florida and southern Europe insurance markets partially nationalised
Fed caps 10-year yield informally via 'market functioning' purchases; financial repression becomes de facto policy across G7
Quarantine eases into tense armed standoff; firms rush 'friend-shored' fabs in US, Japan, India funded with deficit spending
Sahel-to-Horn conflict belt widens: Ethiopia-Eritrea war and a Serbia-Kosovo flare-up count as new major conflicts alongside the Taiwan crisis
EU agrees second joint-debt package for defence and energy; renewable and grid build-out accelerates as energy security, not climate, becomes the rationale
AI adoption recovers on cost-cutting imperative; back-office, call-centre and paralegal jobs shed at scale in rich economies
Italy needs ECB-backed enhanced conditions program after populist budget; riots in Rome and Paris over pension cuts
World growth limps back to 2.4%; inflation settles near 4% with real rates held negative to erode debt
Global public debt reaches ~109% of GDP; US at 141% with interest costs above defence spending
Warming hits 1.61C on the annual average; record South Asian heatwave kills over 40,000
G20 summit fails; rival BRICS-plus clearing system handles ~18% of global trade
Anti-incumbent movements win in four G7 countries over 2029-31; trust in institutions at multi-decade lows

winners: Defence contractors and friend-shored chipmakers (US, Japan, India)
Gulf-independent energy exporters: US LNG, Norway, Brazil, Canada
Owners of real assets and AI-heavy incumbent firms that survived the capex bust
losers: Import-dependent low-income countries in Africa and South Asia hit by food, fuel and debt shocks
Young renters and savers in rich countries eroded by financial repression and inflation
Taiwan, Southern Europe and climate-exposed coastal regions
bullets: The world spent five years lurching from shock to shock: an oil spike, a stagflationary recession, a Taiwan quarantine and serial climate disasters.
Advanced-economy bond markets never fully broke, but only because central banks quietly capped yields; financial repression is the new normal.
Nine sovereigns defaulted or restructured, nearly all in the Global South, with little multilateral help.
Trade has split into a US-led and a China-led bloc with high tariffs, sanctioned banks and duplicated supply chains.
Energy security, not climate policy, drove renewables to ~43% of electricity, yet warming still crossed 1.6C.
AI diffusion slowed in the 2028 bust then accelerated as a cost-cutting tool, displacing ~42M jobs and widening inequality.
Politics is angrier and more fragmented: anti-incumbent waves, pension riots and migration backlash dominate.
Insurance retreat from climate-exposed regions has made the state the insurer of last resort, adding to debt.
wildcard: China's 11-week customs quarantine of Taiwan in 2029, halting most advanced-chip exports without a shot fired at the island.
image_description: In a sweltering Milan apartment in July 2031, a family eats dinner by battery lantern during a rolling blackout while a phone on the table pings with a rationing notice and an AI-written letter terminating the father's claims-processing job.
